I build small, self-contained tools when explaining something twice is slower
than making the thing that explains it. Everything here is open and free to use.

#### Which Test, and Why?
An interactive statistical test chooser built for the CLIF Foundational
Workshop at NUS. Decision-first: you describe your data and design, it shows
the appropriate test with worked examples in both R and Python.

[Open the chooser →](https://michelerenard.github.io/clif-chooser/){.no-rule}
:::

::: {.card-item .night}
#### ICEE 2026 programme
A single-page, searchable schedule for the International Conference on
Environmental Ergonomics 2026 in Kuching, with full plenary and symposium
abstracts.

[Open the programme →](https://michelerenard.github.io/icee-2026/){.no-rule}
:::
:::

## Teaching material

**"Which Test, and Why?"** — CLIF Foundational Workshop on Statistical
Approaches, NUS, 28 August 2026. A 60-minute decision-first primer on
statistical test selection for junior research assistants and coordinators.
The workshop is accompanied by the interactive chooser above and a one-page
reference sheet, with all worked examples given in both R and Python.

**Project HEATS interactive workshop** — Indoor Air 2026, Singapore. Featured
speaker with S. Schiavon, R. Mani, W. Zhang and X. Fan, presenting the HEATS
framework for optimising sleep: heat exposure characterisation, protection of
vulnerable groups, technical cooling and behavioural intervention.

## Methods I use, and why

A short, opinionated list — the methods that come up most often in my work and
the problem each one actually solves.

| Method | The problem it solves |
|---|---|
| Linear mixed-effects models | Repeated nights within a person are not independent observations |
| Mundlak within/between decomposition | Separates "hot nights change what people do" from "heat changes what their body does" |
| Segmented / piecewise regression with AIC knot search | Finds where an exposure–response relationship actually bends, rather than assuming it is a straight line |
| Restricted cubic splines | Lets the shape of a dose–response curve be estimated, not imposed |
| Cluster-robust standard errors and cluster bootstrap | Honest uncertainty when observations come in groups |
| PRISMA 2020 / PROSPERO registration | Makes a review's decisions checkable, and its scope fixed before the results are known |

## Software

**`heatsviz`** — contributor to the internal visualisation package used across
Project HEATS, providing a consistent figure grammar and export presets for
manuscripts and slides in both R and Python.

**Reproducible reporting** — most of my analysis pipelines are Python
(statsmodels, pandas, seaborn, python-docx, PyMuPDF) with R for figures
(tidyverse, ggplot2), version controlled in Git and written up in Quarto.
